items.question: What does reading a stored value that is not a known status or old spelling return?
items.ticket: Existing values are normalised when read
items.chose: Returns null instead of throwing or guessing the nearest status.
items.instead: Throw an error, or fall back to a default status such as draft.

items.question: How is a stored value cleaned before it is matched (case, whitespace, separators)?
items.chose: Trims, lowercases, and collapses each run of whitespace, '-' and '_' into one space.
items.instead: Only trim and lowercase, with no separator handling.

items.question: Which old spellings are mapped to a status?
items.ticket: Sandbox status is stored as free text (draft, Draft, in-review...)
items.chose: Maps only 'in review' (the cleaned form of in-review) to review. Every other old spelling, such as 'in progress' or 'done', reads as null.
items.instead: Map more synonyms (for example 'in progress', 'done', 'pr') or accept prefix and fuzzy matches.

items.question: Does writing accept a value that is only a variant of a status, such as 'Draft', ' draft' or 'in-review'?
items.chose: Accepts only the exact lowercase enum strings and throws for everything else, including variants and old spellings.
items.instead: Normalise the value with the read logic and write the canonical status.

items.question: What does writing an invalid value do?
items.chose: Throws an Error whose message is 'not a sandbox status: "<value>"'.
items.instead: Return null or undefined, return a result object, or fall back to a default.

items.question: What does writing an empty string do?
items.chose: Throws, because the empty string is not in the status list.
items.instead: Treat it as unset and write a default such as draft or null.

items.question: What does reading an empty or whitespace-only value return?
When reading many rows, what happens to a row whose status cannot be read?
items.chose: Keeps the row in place with status null and does not drop it or throw.
items.instead: Drop the row, or throw on the first unreadable row.

items.question: How are unreadable values reported by readStatuses (raw or cleaned, duplicates, order)?
items.chose: Lists the raw stored strings (uncleaned), de-duplicated, sorted with the default string sort.
items.instead: List the unreadable row ids, or list the values with duplicates in row order, or cleaned.

items.question: What is the order of the rows returned by readStatuses?
items.chose: Preserves the input order and one output row per input row.
items.instead: Group or sort rows by status or id.

items.question: Are inherited object keys like 'constructor' or '__proto__' treated as statuses?
items.chose: No. Matching uses an array includes and a Map lookup, so these read as null.
items.instead: Use a plain object lookup, which would risk matching prototype keys.

items.question: Where is the enum applied: only in the status module, or at the callers that set status?
items.ticket: use it where the status is set
items.chose: Only adds the read and write helpers in src/index.ts and changes no call sites.
items.instead: Also change the code that sets the status to go through the enum helper.
